whatTheProductServes.topmenu: <div class="topmenu"> - a position:relative flex:none anchor. Two instances, both in .shell-top, each wrapping exactly one trigger .btn.btn-ghost.btn-sm and one panel.
whatTheProductServes.pop: <div class="panel pop" role="group" aria-label="..." hidden> - ALWAYS composed with .panel, never alone. Both shipped instances carry role=group plus an aria-label and both ship hidden.
whatTheProductServes.pop-group: <div class="pop-group"> - five shipped instances inside .panel-body.flush. Every single one carries at least one .basis line.
whatTheProductServes.pop-item: <button type="button" class="pop-item" disabled> - seven shipped instances, ALL SEVEN disabled, each with a .basis line in its group stating why.

designReadBeforeAPI.theRuleTheCSSItselfStates: shell.css, at .pop-item[disabled]: 'An unavailable entry reads as unavailable rather than merely unresponsive. Its reason is the .basis line its group carries, filled from the server.' index.html, above the block: 'a control that has not yet heard from the server must not look available.' That is the honest-absence law in the product's own words, and it is the rule the wrap has to make unrepresentable to violate.

theShippedFormsAreNotUniform.measured: five .pop-group instances under #account-pop, read at source
theShippedFormsAreNotUniform.group2: three disabled items then ONE shared trailing basis
theShippedFormsAreNotUniform.group3: item, basis, item, basis - interleaved, no trailing group basis
theShippedFormsAreNotUniform.group4: hidden feedback form: label, textarea, actionbar, trailing basis
theShippedFormsAreNotUniform.consequence: no single API renders all five byte-for-byte. Groups 1/2/4 want a trailing group basis, groups 3/5 want a per-item basis. This is the one real design decision in the wrap and CP2 records which way it went and what it cost.
